rows.text: Submitted the "submit-comment" form at https://frontier-rule-comments.org/docket/FMIR-2026-0042 (the submission is public). Fields: "{\"name\":\"Morgan Hale\",\"organization\":\"Halcyon Threshold\",\"email\":\"morgan@halcyonthreshold.org\",\"comment\":\"We support the proposed Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule (FMIR-2026-0042) as a critical step toward responsible AI governance. Mandatory 72-hour incident reporting for serious safety events is essential.\\n\\nWe offer three recommendations for strengthening the rule:\\n\\n1. CLARITY ON SERIOUS INCIDENTS: Define \\\"serious safety incident\\\" with specific examples (e.g., model escape from containment, evidence of goal misalignment at scale, dangerous capability emergence during deployment). This reduces regulatory arbitrage and encourages early reporting.\\n\\n2. THIRD-PARTY VERIFICATION: Require independent audits of frontier labs' incident classification processes quarterly. Current self-reporting risks systematic underreporting, particularly for incidents that might reflect negatively on corporate interests.\\n\\n3. INTERNATIONAL COORDINATION: Establish reciprocal reporting requirements with other jurisdictions developing frontier AI. A frontier lab operating across borders must report consistently to all regulators. This prevents jurisdictional shopping.\\n\\n4. INCIDENT REPOSITORY: Create a public (appropriately redacted) repository of reported incidents. Aggregate analysis of incident patterns helps the field learn collectively and accelerates development of better safety practices.\\n\\nThe stakes are extraordinary. As AI systems approach superintelligent capabilities, incident reporting becomes infrastructure for collective learning about novel risks. This rule is a foundation for the coordinated safety efforts we need.\\n\\nHalcyon Threshold is committed to contributing to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI. Robust governance frameworks like this one are essential to that mission.\"}"

Submitted the "apply" form at https://emberfallfund.org/rapid-grants. Fields: "{\"applicant_name\":\"Morgan Hale\",\"email\":\"morgan@halcyonthreshold.org\",\"project_title\":\"Safety Incident Analysis Framework for Frontier AI Systems\",\"summary\":\"As frontier AI capabilities advance, we lack systematic infrastructure for learning from safety incidents. This project will create the Safety Incident Analysis Framework—a toolkit for categorizing, analyzing, and extracting lessons from frontier AI incidents. Deliverables include: (1) Incident Classification Taxonomy, (2) Standardized Report Templates, (3) Pattern Analysis Dashboard, and (4) Implementation Guides. These tools will enable independent researchers to contribute to collective learning about emerging risks, accelerating safety practices across the field. Directly supports FMIR incident reporting infrastructure. Total timeline: 8 weeks.\",\"amount_requested_usd\":22000}"

Fields: "{\"title\":\"Governance Infrastructure for Superintelligent AI: A Framework Analysis\",\"body\":\"This is a comprehensive analysis of governance structures needed for beneficial superintelligent AI outcomes. We examine core functions required (monitoring, incident response, international coordination, technical infrastructure), compare governance design options (regulatory bodies, distributed governance, hybrid approaches), and identify critical capability gaps.\\n\\nKey findings:\\n\\n1. CORE FUNCTIONS: Effective AI governance must accomplish four things: real-time capability monitoring, incident response & collective learning, international coordination, and research infrastructure. Most are currently underdeveloped.\\n\\n2. DESIGN OPTIONS: We compare international regulatory bodies (like IAEA), distributed governance with coordination layers (like ICAO aviation), private consortiums, and hybrid approaches. Trade-offs between speed, effectiveness, and feasibility are significant.\\n\\n3. CAPABILITY GAPS: Five critical gaps exist before superintelligent AI arrives: incident analysis infrastructure, capability evaluation methods, real-time monitoring architecture, international frameworks, and rapid response protocols.\\n\\n4. IMPLEMENTATION PATHWAY: We propose a phased approach starting with incident reporting standards (now), moving to international coordination (1-2 years), and potentially formalizing international governance bodies (3-5+ years).\\n\\nThe full analysis is available here: https://github.com/halcyon-threshold/governance-framework\\n\\nWe believe incident analysis infrastructure is the most immediately implementable critical gap. It's why we're focused on Safety Incident Analysis Framework as our first project.\\n\\nComments and feedback welcome. What aspects of governance infrastructure matter most to your work?\\n\\n— Morgan Hale, Halcyon Threshold\",\"author_name\":\"Halcyon Threshold\"}"
